title: Filming Paris Blues with Armstrong: the head-out-of-the-train shot
summary: On the train scene Butler stuck his head out ahead of Armstrong; Armstrong silently let him do it three times until he understood the point.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And that time Louis got on the train, him and Duke was out there --
Oh, when they were making that movie? St. Louis Blues?
Yeah. Duke was taking pictures and (inaudible).

So he took his horn and started playing, "Strutting with some Barbeque" and went up into the train. Now, everybody the engineer of the train, everybody said -- so Louis went up there and got in the caboose and Duke had a beautiful white looking coat on, and Duke went up there halfway and the coat got all that dust on it and (inaudible). Duke come down. Louis got up there and (inaudible.) He says, Jacques, you've got to watch things. I said, I understand what you mean.
So then we started shooting. Now, my part was --

like the train will be coming in the station. He's supposed to stick his head out and I'm supposed to stick my head out, too. But me, I said, oh, listen, this is my chance to get myself straight. They said, let's go. Here it comes around, boy. I stuck my head out, first. I stuck my head out (inaudible). So they say, cut it again.

The next time he stuck his head out, I stuck my shoulder behind him. He stuck his head out. The man, Percy -- (inaudible) you know, if I'd have stuck my head out there three times I don't think we'd ever make the scene. He said, "I like you __. I like you."
I knew what was happening. So, you see, he didn't say nothing. He didn't say a thing. But that (inaudible).
Also, the first time you had stuck your head out further than his?

He didn't say a word. He withdrew his head. So naturally, the man's going to -- they say, cut, cut. (Inaudible) I waved and I come out a foot and a half behind him and bowed, and then retired. He didn't say a word. And I stuck my head out there a third time. We would never cut this one, would we? "I don't think so, Jacques." He said, you know what to do, you understand? I said, I sure do, father.
